summary.text: Abdul El-Sayed is a physician and public health official who became Detroit's health director in 2015, ran for governor in 2018 and led the Wayne County health department from 2022 to 2025. He is the Democratic nominee for the open Michigan Senate seat after winning the August 4, 2026 primary over Rep. Haley Stevens, and his campaign says he is running to make life in Michigan less expensive, including through Medicare for All.

paragraphs.text: Abdul El-Sayed was born and raised in Southeast Michigan and attended public schools, where he captained his high school football, wrestling and lacrosse teams. His campaign biography says his father, Mohamed, is an Egyptian immigrant and that he was raised with his stepmother, Jackie.

He graduated from the University of Michigan in 2007 with a B.S. in biology and political science and played on its men's lacrosse team. He earned a D.Phil. in public health from the University of Oxford in 2011 as a Rhodes Scholar and an M.D. from Columbia University in 2014, then became an assistant professor of epidemiology at Columbia.
After Detroit's bankruptcy, El-Sayed was hired in 2015 to manage the city's newly privatized health department, a post he held until February 2017, when he left to run for governor full time.
His campaign credits him with securing free glasses for children, removing lead from elementary schools and making Narcan universally accessible.
He lost the August 7, 2018 Democratic primary for governor to Gretchen Whitmer, receiving 30.2% of the vote, and afterward served on several boards and as a political adviser and contributor.
In 2020 El-Sayed was selected for President Biden's Unity Task Force on healthcare, and he is the author of Medicare for All: A Citizen's Guide.

From 2022 to 2025 he was director and health officer of the Wayne County Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services, where his campaign says he spearheaded a program to cancel up to $700 million in medical debt for 300,000 residents.
With Sen. Gary Peters not seeking re-election, El-Sayed won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 48.5% to Stevens' 47.5%; Mallory McMorrow, who had unofficially withdrawn, received 4.0%.
He faces Republican Mike Rogers in the general election, and according to his campaign website he lives in Ann Arbor with his wife, Sarah, and their two daughters.
